methodological_findings: Procedural reports can bundle facts from different occurrence dates; event identity must be reconstructed before classification.
A source-reported exact count is not sufficient to mint individual event IDs.
Two events in the same night remain distinct when premises/locations are distinct, even when investigated in one operation.
Two adjacent targets during one uninterrupted sequence may be one continuous episode; target multiplicity alone does not force event splitting.
Operation date and operation geography are procedural attributes, not occurrence attributes.
Recent reporting on historical judgments is a useful locator but not a substitute for the primary judicial/archival source.
